questions.stem: This axial abdominal CT shows a contrast-filled aorta surrounded by a large collection of extraluminal material tracking into the retroperitoneum. What life-threatening event is depicted?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ruptured aortic aneurysm with retroperitoneal hemorrhage

choices.label: C
choices.text: Contained aortic dissection with intimal flap

choices.label: E
choices.text: Renal cell carcinoma invading the aorta

explanation.summary: The bright contrast-filled aorta with an adjacent large blood collection extending into the retroperitoneum indicates a ruptured aortic aneurysm, a surgical emergency with high mortality.
explanation.whyCorrect: The bright contrast-filled aorta with an adjacent large blood collection extending into the retroperitoneum indicates a ruptured aortic aneurysm, a surgical emergency with high mortality.

questions.stem: A clinician places both hands on the patient's mid-abdomen as shown. What physical exam finding is being sought to screen for an abdominal aortic aneurysm?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A pulsatile, expansile midline abdominal mass

choices.label: B
choices.text: A palpable spleen tip below the costal margin

explanation.summary: AAA is classically detected as a pulsatile, laterally expansile mass in the epigastrium/periumbilical region on bimanual palpation, though sensitivity is limited in obese patients.
explanation.whyCorrect: AAA is classically detected as a pulsatile, laterally expansile mass in the epigastrium/periumbilical region on bimanual palpation, though sensitivity is limited in obese patients.

questions.stem: This transverse aortic ultrasound (measured at 7.46 cm) demonstrates a channel of flow separated from the true lumen alongside layered mural material. What does the labeled 'false lumen' finding most strongly indicate?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Aortic dissection, where blood has entered a channel within the vessel wall

choices.label: C
choices.text: A normal aorta with reverberation artifact

choices.label: D
choices.text: Simple venous thrombosis adjacent to the aorta

explanation.summary: A false lumen separated from the true lumen by an intimal flap is the hallmark of aortic dissection; the enlarged diameter and intraluminal thrombus reflect an associated aneurysmal, dissected aorta.
explanation.whyCorrect: A false lumen separated from the true lumen by an intimal flap is the hallmark of aortic dissection; the enlarged diameter and intraluminal thrombus reflect an associated aneurysmal, dissected aorta.

questions.stem: Comparing these two axial CT images, the right-hand aorta is markedly dilated with a crescent of low-density material lining its wall around a smaller central contrast column. What is that crescentic lining?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mural (laminated) thrombus within the aneurysm sac

choices.label: E
choices.text: An intramural hematoma of a dissection

explanation.summary: Enlarged aortic aneurysms commonly contain laminated mural thrombus lining the sac, leaving only a smaller central patent lumen through which contrast flows, as contrasted with the normal-caliber aorta on the left.
explanation.whyCorrect: Enlarged aortic aneurysms commonly contain laminated mural thrombus lining the sac, leaving only a smaller central patent lumen through which contrast flows, as contrasted with the normal-caliber aorta on the left.

questions.stem: This semi-erect chest radiograph pair highlights a mediastinal contour measuring 12.5 cm (normal 6-8 cm). In a patient with chest/back pain, this finding should raise immediate suspicion for what?

choices.label: E
choices.text: Thoracic aortic aneurysm or aortic dissection

explanation.summary: A widened mediastinum on chest X-ray is a classic red flag for thoracic aortic pathology (aneurysm/dissection) and mandates urgent CT angiography to confirm.
explanation.whyCorrect: A widened mediastinum on chest X-ray is a classic red flag for thoracic aortic pathology (aneurysm/dissection) and mandates urgent CT angiography to confirm.

questions.stem: These angiographic and CT images show a metallic mesh device conforming to the curve of the thoracic aorta. What intervention is depicted?

explanation.summary: The radiopaque stent-graft lining the aortic lumen indicates endovascular aneurysm repair, which excludes the aneurysm sac from arterial pressure via a covered stent deployed through a catheter.
explanation.whyCorrect: The radiopaque stent-graft lining the aortic lumen indicates endovascular aneurysm repair, which excludes the aneurysm sac from arterial pressure via a covered stent deployed through a catheter.

questions.stem: On this unlabeled axial abdominal CT, the structure immediately anterior to the vertebral body shows a rounded soft-tissue rim surrounding a smaller central lumen. What does this appearance most likely represent?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A dilated loop of small bowel

choices.label: D
choices.text: Abdominal aortic aneurysm with mural thrombus

explanation.summary: A rounded, dilated prevertebral aortic contour with a thick low-density rim (mural thrombus) around a smaller patent lumen is the classic CT appearance of an abdominal aortic aneurysm.
explanation.whyCorrect: A rounded, dilated prevertebral aortic contour with a thick low-density rim (mural thrombus) around a smaller patent lumen is the classic CT appearance of an abdominal aortic aneurysm.

questions.stem: Panel B shows a color Doppler ultrasound with a swirling red/blue 'yin-yang' flow pattern connected by a narrow neck to the femoral artery, following a groin catheterization. What is this finding?

explanation.summary: The 'yin-yang' swirling flow with a to-and-fro neck communicating with the femoral artery is the classic Doppler signature of a pseudoaneurysm, a common complication of arterial puncture.
explanation.whyCorrect: The 'yin-yang' swirling flow with a to-and-fro neck communicating with the femoral artery is the classic Doppler signature of a pseudoaneurysm, a common complication of arterial puncture.

questions.stem: This patient's toes show painful, well-demarcated bluish-purple discoloration despite palpable pulses. In the setting of an aortic aneurysm, what is the most likely mechanism?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Deep vein thrombosis of the leg

choices.label: D
choices.text: Atheroembolism (cholesterol emboli) occluding small digital arteries

explanation.summary: Blue toe syndrome results from showers of atheromatous/cholesterol emboli from a proximal aneurysm or atherosclerotic aorta lodging in digital vessels, producing painful cyanotic toes with preserved proximal pulses.
explanation.whyCorrect: Blue toe syndrome results from showers of atheromatous/cholesterol emboli from a proximal aneurysm or atherosclerotic aorta lodging in digital vessels, producing painful cyanotic toes with preserved proximal pulses.

questions.stem: This cumulative curve plots proportion ruptured against aneurysm diameter for two sexes (P<.001). What are the two key teaching points it conveys?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Rupture risk is independent of diameter for both sexes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Rupture occurs only above 10 cm regardless of sex

choices.label: C
choices.text: Men rupture at consistently smaller diameters than women

choices.label: D
choices.text: Diameter and sex have no statistically significant effect

choices.label: E
choices.text: Rupture risk rises steeply with diameter, and women rupture at smaller diameters than men

explanation.summary: Rupture risk increases markedly with aneurysm diameter, and the women's curve is shifted left, indicating rupture at smaller diameters, which supports lower repair thresholds in women.
explanation.whyCorrect: Rupture risk increases markedly with aneurysm diameter, and the women's curve is shifted left, indicating rupture at smaller diameters, which supports lower repair thresholds in women.

questions.stem: The illustration shows a spindle-shaped dilation of the artery behind the knee, paired with a clinical exam of the same region. Beyond rupture, what is the most characteristic complication of this particular aneurysm?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Distal thromboembolism and acute limb ischemia

explanation.summary: Popliteal artery aneurysms rupture less often than they thrombose or shed emboli; their major threat is acute or chronic limb ischemia from thrombosis and distal embolization.
explanation.whyCorrect: Popliteal artery aneurysms rupture less often than they thrombose or shed emboli; their major threat is acute or chronic limb ischemia from thrombosis and distal embolization.

questions.stem: The right side of this figure contrasts two aneurysm shapes on a vessel wall. What structural feature distinguishes a saccular aneurysm from a fusiform one?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Saccular aneurysms occur only in veins; fusiform only in arteries

choices.label: B
choices.text: Saccular aneurysms are always false aneurysms; fusiform are always true

choices.label: C
choices.text: The two terms describe the same shape at different sizes

choices.label: D
choices.text: A saccular aneurysm is an eccentric outpouching of one side of the wall, whereas a fusiform aneurysm dilates the entire circumference

choices.label: E
choices.text: A saccular aneurysm involves the whole circumference; fusiform involves one wall

explanation.summary: Fusiform aneurysms are symmetric, circumferential dilations of the vessel, while saccular aneurysms are asymmetric, berry-like outpouchings involving only part of the wall circumference.
explanation.whyCorrect: Fusiform aneurysms are symmetric, circumferential dilations of the vessel, while saccular aneurysms are asymmetric, berry-like outpouchings involving only part of the wall circumference.

questions.stem: This figure contrasts a normal vessel, two true aneurysms, and a false aneurysm. What defines a false aneurysm (pseudoaneurysm) as shown on the right?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Dilation confined entirely within a normal endothelium

choices.label: B
choices.text: A contained rupture where blood is held by surrounding tissue rather than all three intact vessel-wall layers

choices.label: C
choices.text: Symmetric dilation involving all three intact wall layers

choices.label: D
choices.text: An outpouching lined by an intact intima and media only

choices.label: E
choices.text: A congenital absence of the tunica adventitia

explanation.summary: A true aneurysm involves dilation of all three attenuated wall layers, whereas a false aneurysm is a contained rupture: blood escapes the wall and is held by adventitia/perivascular tissue and hematoma.
explanation.whyCorrect: A true aneurysm involves dilation of all three attenuated wall layers, whereas a false aneurysm is a contained rupture: blood escapes the wall and is held by adventitia/perivascular tissue and hematoma.

questions.stem: This illustration shows a balloon-like dilation of the aorta just above the heart, with an inset magnifying the affected segment. Given this location, what serious complication is most characteristic if it dilates the aortic root?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Aortic valve regurgitation from stretching of the valve annulus

explanation.summary: A thoracic (ascending/root) aortic aneurysm can dilate the aortic annulus, splaying the valve leaflets and producing aortic regurgitation, in addition to risks of dissection and rupture.
explanation.whyCorrect: A thoracic (ascending/root) aortic aneurysm can dilate the aortic annulus, splaying the valve leaflets and producing aortic regurgitation, in addition to risks of dissection and rupture.

questions.stem: Panels B and C show two ways of treating the infrarenal aortic dilation in panel A. Compared with the technique in panel B, what is the principal advantage of the catheter-delivered approach in panel C?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It avoids a major open laparotomy and aortic cross-clamping, so it is less invasive with faster recovery

choices.label: B
choices.text: It removes the aneurysm sac entirely from the body

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is preferred because it fully restores the native aortic diameter

choices.label: D
choices.text: It eliminates any future need for imaging surveillance

choices.label: E
choices.text: It permanently cures the underlying degeneration of the aortic wall

explanation.summary: Panel A is an abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA). Panel B is open surgical repair with an interposition graft (laparotomy, clamping). Panel C is endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR), in which a covered stent-graft is deployed via the femoral arteries to exclude the sac from arterial pressure, offering lower perioperative morbidity but requiring lifelong surveillance for endoleak.
explanation.whyCorrect: Panel A is an abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA). Panel B is open surgical repair with an interposition graft (laparotomy, clamping). Panel C is endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR), in which a covered stent-graft is deployed via the femoral arteries to exclude the sac from arterial pressure, offering lower perioperative morbidity but requiring lifelong surveillance for endoleak.
